mechanism_narrative: The sustained decline in RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks indicates a persistent trend of reduced non-essential activity, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks as restrictions likely remain.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, indicating a reversal of the observed trend.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains consistently high, it signifies a strong adherence to stay-at-home directives or preferences, directly suppressing retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 15% for two consecutive weeks (t-1w and t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 15% for the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined sharp decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility suggests a significant reduction in commuting and office presence, which will severely limit incidental retail and recreation trips over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, even with TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, a decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility indicates a broader reduction in essential outings, which will further depress non-essential RETAIL_REC activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -5% at t-0w and continues to decline week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases, despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent and steep decline in TRANSIT mobility reflects a widespread reduction in public transport usage, directly translating to fewer people moving around and visiting retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, while TRANSIT mobility remains below -60%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in PARKS mobility, especially after a period of relative stability, suggests a heightened public caution or stricter outdoor gathering rules, which will negatively impact RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 20 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases, despite PARKS mobility remaining low.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse relationship where RESIDENTIAL mobility rises significantly while WORKPLACES mobility falls sharply indicates a strong shift towards working from home and staying home, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases, even with RESIDENTIAL remaining high and WORKPLACES remaining low.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of sustained restrictions, the inability of WORKPLACES mobility to recover, staying below -30%, signifies ongoing business closures or remote work mandates, which will prevent RETAIL_REC from improving over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks (t-1w and t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining below -30%.
